sources.title: Instituto Socioambiental: Yanomami
sources.note: Direct full entry: Localização e população, Os antigos Yanomami and Primeiros contatos. Retain uncertainty of early nineteenth-century dispersal and avoid outdated four-language classification.

sources.title: Brazil Casa Civil: Terra Indígena Yanomami
sources.note: Direct page, Onde vivem and Históricos de contato; 1992 recognition, separate Ye’kwana identity, 1973 road and 1980s mining. No current population estimate adopted.

sources.title: UNICEF: Education for life the Yanomami way, Brazil
sources.note: OHCHR-hosted UNICEF teaching resource, printed p.86. Direct PDF fetch failed; indexed original returned full page with query site.searchlibrary.ohchr.org/ "Education for life the Yanomami way" "family". Particular portrait of Kiko, not universal household or current survey.

sources.title: Smithsonian Human Studies Film Archives: A Man and his Wife Weave a Hammock
sources.note: Direct fetch failed; indexed original full record checked with exact title and site.si.edu query. HSFA 1984.16.11, 1974 edited film from 1971 project. Catalogue description checked, film not viewed.

sources.title: Sanöma teachers and research partners: Ana amopö, Cogumelos (2016)
sources.note: Direct fetch failed; original indexed PDF returned cover, copyright 2016 and printed p.9. Reproducible queries site.acervo.socioambiental.org "Ana amopö" "Cogumelos" and "Enciclopédia" "cogumelos" "roças". Cover gives exact Sanöma/Portuguese title; English translation supplied. Catalogue and PDF treated as one work.

sources.title: INPA / PPBio: Women from Maturacá describe a fungus used in basketry
sources.note: Direct institutional report, paragraphs below heading. Kumirãyôma women, shiny black fungal strands, Marasmius yanomami, collaborative bilingual book. No universal claim of sole world users adopted.

sources.title: Hutukara Associação Yanomami: Arte Yanomami, Cestaria (2025)
sources.note: Direct fetch failed; full indexed original printed pp.6 to 7, Caminho da cestaria. Specific basket forms, gender attribution, transfer through Hutukara and community-requested goods.

sources.title: Fiotec / Fiocruz: Mercury study in nine Ninam villages (2024)
sources.note: Direct 5 June 2024 report. Samples collected October 2022 in Alto Rio Mucajaí; 287 hair samples. Preserve study scope, no population-wide inference or medical advice.

sources.title: Brazil Ministry of Indigenous Peoples: Territorial monitoring workshop (2025)
sources.note: Direct fetch failed; full indexed original via exact title. Published 12 September 2025, workshop 11 to 27 August in Palimiú and Maloca Paapiú. Distinguishes community monitoring from state enforcement.

sources.title: Yurok Tribe: Our history
sources.note: Direct page extraction omitted some body text; complete indexed original read using site.yuroktribe.org/our-history "dentalia". Villages, river foods, family houses and shell money. Avoid stale present-day population/employment figures.

sources.title: National Park Service: Redwood area history
sources.note: Direct Indigenous People section: politically independent linked villages, regional plankhouse design, 1850 gold rush and state-supported violence. Regional house detail explicitly attributed as regional; does not merge neighbouring peoples.

sources.title: Constitution of the Yurok Tribe (1993)
sources.note: Direct original PDF, p.1 ratified 19 November 1993, preamble and articles describing government. Modern constitutional institutions distinguished from older village organisation.

sources.title: Redwood National and State Parks: The making of a Yurok canoe
sources.note: Direct two-page government brochure on public NPS History mirror. Page 1 named 1968 carvers/display canoe and water preventing cracking; page 2 log orientation and river navigation.

sources.title: National Museum of the American Indian: Yurok cooking basket, 14/5526
sources.note: Direct museum catalogue. Yurok, willow/conifer root/beargrass, twined, donated by Helen Culver Kerr in 1926; no manufacture date or named maker. Northern California location is explicitly inferred.

sources.title: Cultural Fire Management Council: Projects
sources.note: Direct primary organisation account: Fire Program, Family Burning, Native Plant Study and Education. No restricted harvest maps accessed.

sources.title: Yurok Tribe: Yurok language curriculum
sources.note: Direct Curriculum heading exact Kee-tue skuue-lek’ rendered with ASCII apostrophe on source, paired with I’m going to school! Also graded lessons and archive description.

sources.title: Yurok Tribe: Language programme launches new project (2022)
sources.note: Direct dated 10 January 2022 report, Planting Seeds. Acorn gathering/eel-hook making already organised; digital resources proposed. No claim that all planned components were completed.

sources.title: Yurok Tribe: Revegetation work behind former Klamath dams (2024)
sources.note: Full indexed primary report, 11 October 2024. In-river removal completed 2 October; native seeds, plants, insect food and salmon return. Avoid single-cause numerical salmon decline attribution.
